principles: One-shot convergence without rerunning project commands
Fail closed outside the exact canonical lifecycle transaction
drivers: Remove the observed mandatory manual metadata commit and retry
Preserve canonical PASS receipt integrity and CAS semantics
Keep the patch narrow enough for focused adversarial review

options.name: A: transition-owned atomic closeout
pros: Makes the lifecycle transition finish clean before mandatory validate
Avoids teaching verifier to adopt pre-existing dirty state
cons: May couple phase advancement to validation-specific artifacts
Could alter closeout ordering beyond the observed path

options.name: B: receipt-bound reuse transaction admission
pros: Keeps reuse persistence in the existing isolated CAS writer
Can atomically include only causally proven generated lifecycle paths
cons: Requires a strong canonical writer/receipt classifier
A weak event-shape check would create a bypass

options.name: C: permit metadata-only dirty paths generically
cons: Would absorb human, forged or unrelated lifecycle metadata

rationale: The verifier already owns the reused PASS persistence transaction. Extend that transaction only with dirty lifecycle metadata that existing canonical provenance proves belongs to the immediately preceding authorized flow; otherwise refuse exactly as today. If investigation shows no adequate proof primitive, fall back to option A rather than weakening trust.

preMortem.scenario: A forged process event is admitted because it resembles story_advance output.
preMortem.trigger: Admission checks only path, event type or prose.
preMortem.consequence: An external edit is silently committed as trusted metadata.
preMortem.mitigation: Require canonical receipt/causal writer binding and retain the human_confirmation/direct-edit negative controls.

preMortem.scenario: The fix hides concurrent or hook-generated changes inside the metadata commit.
preMortem.trigger: Transaction capture occurs after untrusted dirt or does not verify exact index paths and HEAD CAS.
preMortem.consequence: Unrelated changes become part of a validation PASS commit.
preMortem.mitigation: Capture before authorized writes, verify exact managed path set, preserve index bytes, and keep concurrent-HEAD/hook mutation tests.

preMortem.scenario: The RED passes without traversing the production lifecycle boundary.
preMortem.trigger: The test directly calls a helper or manually cleans metadata before reuse.
preMortem.consequence: B-0784 behavior remains broken despite green unit tests.
preMortem.mitigation: Run real local CLI story transition followed immediately by validate and assert a single successful invocation plus a clean tree.

preMortem.scenario: Every TEST transition starts auto-committing arbitrary metadata and invalidates review evidence again.
preMortem.trigger: Writer ordering or hash binding changes too broadly.
preMortem.consequence: The fix trades one retry for repeated review re-attestation.
preMortem.mitigation: Limit committed paths to canonical generated metadata, assert trusted metadata-descendant lineage, and check review/storyFiles hashes remain admissible.
